title: Portrait and Cipher
premise: Zephyrine Ishikawa, the coroner of Grayhollow, is handed a missing person's diary belonging to Lark Voss, vanished a year ago — but its final entries are dated after her disappearance and describe his own investigation in unnerving detail. As Zephyrine follows the diary's cipher toward an inheritance hidden beneath the town's founding families, he realizes the killer is someone with access to every case file: his own deputy. At the anniversary dinner honoring Lark's memory, Zephyrine springs his trap, exposing Deputy Cora Bell as Lark's half-sister, who killed to claim the Voss fortune — and survived by learning to read everyone like a case file.
about_author: Petra Dravenmoor spent a decade as a rural records clerk before turning to crime fiction, giving her novels their obsession with paperwork, small towns, and the dead who refuse to stay filed away. She writes from a farmhouse full of inherited furniture she has never once trusted.

chapters.title: The Diary That Kept Writing
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. A fisherman finds Lark Voss's diary wedged in a culvert; its last entry is dated three weeks after she vanished and describes Zephyrine opening this very drawer. He rereads every cold-case file that night, unable to sleep. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional curiosity — the moment a man who names graves realizes one may be naming him.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, with a flashback chapter from Lark's diary interleaved. Zephyrine walks the cemetery, reconstructing Lark's final documented week, and notices her grave plot was purchased anonymously two days before she disappeared. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion as he realizes the town mourned a woman someone had already planned to bury.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The diary's margins hold a numeric cipher keyed to cemetery plot numbers; decoded fragments point to the Voss family crypt and an unrecorded will. His deputy, Cora Bell, volunteers eagerly to help transcribe pages. Emotional beat: cautious hope — for the first time the case feels solvable, which is exactly what someone wants him to feel.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: POV alternating Zephyrine and Cora. Preparations begin for the town's memorial dinner marking one year since Lark's disappearance; Cora chairs it with unsettling devotion. Zephyrine notes Cora quoted a case detail never made public. Emotional beat: creeping isolation — the colleague he trusts most keeps being one step ahead of him.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Kept
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Inside the Voss crypt he finds a sealed second will leaving everything to an unnamed illegitimate child, plus a photograph of Lark as an infant held by a woman wearing a deputy's academy pin. Someone locks him in overnight among the coffins. Emotional beat: terror and revelation braided together — the inheritance has a living claimant, and she knows he knows.

chapters.title: Duty's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Cora. Her chapters reveal her childhood as the secret Voss daughter, raised poor while Lark inherited everything, and her meticulous plan to erase both sister and evidence. She drafts Zephyrine's obituary 'in case.' Emotional beat: chilling sympathy — Cora believes survival is a debt she is finally collecting, and love was always a currency she couldn't afford.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Forensic analysis proves the post-disappearance diary entries were written in two hands — Lark's under duress, then Cora's imitation. Zephyrine realizes the killer fed him the diary deliberately, to steer the cipher hunt and implicate the town patriarch instead. Emotional beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve — he decides to let the trap close around himself.

chapters.title: Bait in the Case File
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. He plants a falsified report claiming the original will surfaced and names a different heir, logging it in the shared case system only Cora can access. He tells no one, not even the sheriff. Emotional beat: cold courage — the man who catalogs the dead now uses himself as the record others will try to alter.

chapters.title: A Toast at Grayhollow
chapters.summary: POV alternating rapidly between Zephyrine and Cora at the anniversary dinner. Cora takes the bait, lures Zephyrine to the crypt during the toast, and confesses while preparing to stage his suicide beside Lark's remains — unaware the sheriff, tipped via a note hidden in the diary itself, is listening from the dark. Emotional beat: climax of love against duty — Cora hesitates over the knife because Zephyrine was the only one who ever said her name kindly.

chapters.title: Closed File
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine, epilogue months later. Cora confesses fully rather than let her mother take blame; Lark is reburied under her own name, and Zephyrine adds both sisters' stories to his ledger of graves. He keeps the diary, last page blank now. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — survival was paid for, inheritance returned to dust, and duty finally aligned with mercy.
